body.statement: Can the local handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be developed into an algorithm running in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\) that evaluates or approximates \(\widehat\tau_G\) from \((G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}))\), and returns an observable certificate \(U_G\) satisfying \[\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le U_G?\] Can such a certificate either establish \(U_G=O(r(n,d))\) on a probability-\(1-o(1)\) random-regular graph event, or furnish a rigorous obstruction to \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\), while numerical approximation error contributes \(o(r(n,d))\)? If a balanced-hole lower edge at scale \(r(n,d)\) is separately established, an affirmative compiler and \(O(n/k)\) certificate could potentially close the resulting logarithmic bracket for \(R_2(G)\) and make the capsule deployable; it would not implement an already established matched minimax theorem. Both the polynomial-time algorithmic construction and the capsule spectral bound remain open, and the proved upper bound uses a different published Conflict Graph Design.
body.justification: Exact enumeration proves finite evaluability on the positive-inclusion domain but does not deliver a scalable estimator or risk certificate for large networks.
body.gap: No inverse-polynomial overlap or observed-assignment-fiber bound, approximate-counting theorem, or operator-norm certification argument is available from the frozen primitives.
body.consumer: If the balanced-hole lower edge is first established, a successful compiler together with an \(O(n/k)\) capsule certificate could potentially close the resulting logarithmic bracket and make the capsule deployable; it would not implement an already matched minimax theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a polynomial-time observed-data approximation to \(\widehat\tau_G\) and an observable operator-norm risk certificate valid uniformly over \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\), with numerical contribution \(o(r(n,d))\); separately prove \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\) on the required random-regular event or certify an obstruction.
obligation.obstruction: Exact enumeration is finite but exponential. Simulation error bounds depend on an inverse-polynomial lower bound for \(\min_u\pi_u\), while simulation of the Rao--Blackwell ratio also depends on the probability of the realized assignment fiber. Neither lower bound, nor a contraction, mixing-time, approximate-counting, or deterministic spectral certificate, is supplied by the frozen primitives.
obligation.attempted: I extended the finite-enumeration reduction with simultaneous Chebyshev bounds for all inclusion and joint-inclusion probabilities and an explicit entrywise-to-operator-norm conversion. This gives pointwise approximation when positive overlap is quantitatively known, but does not control the conditional Rao--Blackwell fiber or furnish the required uniform polynomial bound.
obligation.partial_result:
For every fixed finite \(G\), finite enumeration computes all inclusion probabilities and detects zero inclusion; when \(p:=\min_u\pi_u>0\), it computes \(\Gamma_G\), \(\widetilde\tau_G\), and \(\widehat\tau_G\) exactly.  There is also a pointwise simulation audit.  Fix an integer \(m\ge1\), draw \(m\) independent copies from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\), and define \(q_{uv}:=\mathbb E[X_uX_v\mid G]\), \(\widehat\pi_u=m^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^mX_u^{(s)}\), and \(\widehat q_{uv}=m^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^mX_u^{(s)}X_v^{(s)}\).  All probabilities in this paragraph are conditional on the fixed \(G\).  Independence and the fact that a Bernoulli variance is at most \(1/4\) give \(\mathbb E[(\widehat\pi_u-\pi_u)^2\mid G]\le1/(4m)\), and the same bound holds for \(\widehat q_{uv}-q_{uv}\).  On the event \(|W|>\varepsilon\), one has \(W^2>\varepsilon^2\), so \(\varepsilon^2\Pr(|W|>\varepsilon\mid G)\le\mathbb E[W^2\mid G]\).  Applying this elementary inequality and then summing the event probabilities over \(2n\) indices or \(4n^2\) ordered pairs gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\max_u|\widehat\pi_u-\pi_u|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{n}{2m\varepsilon^2},
 \qquad
 \Pr\!\left(\max_{u,v}|\widehat q_{uv}-q_{uv}|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{n^2}{m\varepsilon^2}. \tag{4}
\]
If \(\varepsilon\le p/2\), then every \(\widehat\pi_u\ge p/2\).  On this event define
\[
 \widehat\Gamma_{uv}
 :=s_as_b\left\{\frac{\widehat q_{uv}}
 {\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v}-1\right\},
 \qquad u=(i,a),\quad v=(j,b).
\]
Since \(0\le q_{uv}\le1\), direct subtraction of the two normalized ratios gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat q_{uv}}{\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v}
       -\frac{q_{uv}}{\pi_u\pi_v}\right|
 \le \frac{4\varepsilon}{p^2}
 +\frac{|\pi_u\pi_v-\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v|}
 {\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v\pi_u\pi_v}
 \le \frac{4\varepsilon}{p^2}+\frac{8\varepsilon}{p^4}.
\]
Substitution in the normalized-kernel formula and the bound of an operator norm by the largest absolute row sum now yield
\[
 \max_{u,v}|\widehat\Gamma_{uv}-\Gamma_{uv}|
 \le \frac{4\varepsilon}{p^2}+\frac{8\varepsilon}{p^4}
 \le \frac{12\varepsilon}{p^4},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le \frac{24n\varepsilon}{p^4}. \tag{5}
\]
Thus pointwise covariance-action approximation is explicit, but its sample guarantee depends on an a priori lower bound for \(p\), which the unresolved capsule-kernel question does not provide.  Moreover, rejection-based simulation of the conditional ratio defining \(\widehat\tau_G\) depends on the probability of the realized assignment fiber, for which no inverse-polynomial lower bound is available.  Finally, an additive entrywise estimate is not by itself the requested uniform risk certificate: over the endpoint \(L^2\) ball, an \(o(r(n,d))\) risk error requires operator-norm error \(o(nr(n,d))\).  Hence (4)--(5) give a computable fixed-instance audit but not the requested uniform polynomial-time compiler.
